verdict.rationale: Sentry documents a self-hosted option that runs all of Sentry on your own server for free, and community users confirm running it successfully, so a local or dev instance is possible. The docs describe it as a minimal setup with no guarantees or dedicated support. One community report says it grew to consume a 32GB server, and another notes self-hosted releases lag behind the SaaS, both real limits for a lightweight local dev loop. missing for 10: a documented lightweight local/dev-mode setup, explicit evidence that dashboards and instrumentation testing work in the self-hosted instance, guaranteed or supported parity with SaaS, and reasonable resource requirements for local use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases. This version comes with no guarantees or dedicated support.
They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid.
